civic

SIV-ik · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Having to do with citizens, their town, and its shared public life.

Voting is a civic duty for every adult citizen.

Example

Our class did a civic project: we planted flowers along the public path by the library.

The flowers were not for one kid's yard - they were for a path the whole town uses. Work that serves the community you live in is civic.

How civic sits among its neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

public

public: shared by everyone in a community

shared

shared: belonging to the whole group

Antonyms

private

private: for one person only, not for everyone

personal

personal: belonging just to you

How Strong Is It?

helpful → civic → patriotic

helpful vs. civic

helpful vs. civic: Helpful is the milder word: helping means doing something kind for one person, while civic means caring for the shared life of the whole town and all its citizens.

patriotic vs. civic

patriotic vs. civic: Patriotic goes further than civic: civic feeling is pride and care for your own town, while patriotic feeling is that same pride stretched to cover the whole country.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — civ: citizen

suffix — ic: having to do with

Put it together: Civ means citizen, so civic simply means 'having to do with citizens' - the people of a town and the things they all share.

Use the root in a new word: civilian: Civic comes from the Latin root civ-, meaning 'citizen' — in ancient Rome, a civis was a member of the city. English built civilian from the same root. When the air base holds its yearly open day, thousands of civilians stream in to watch the jets take off.
